BCC will host a summit exploring practical applications of artificial intelligence for nonprofit organizations on Nov. 18.

PITTSFIELD — The Workforce and Community Education department at Berkshire Community College will present “AI for Nonprofits,” part of the Berkshire Summit Signature Series, from 8:30 a.m. to 12:30 p.m. Nov. 18, in the Koussevitzky Arts Center, 1350 West St.

The summit will explore practical applications of artificial intelligence, including market research, knowledge management and software development. Speakers include Dennis Iodice of Berkshire Mountain Bakery, Samuel Pascual of Pittsfield Community Television and education and research consultant Stacey M. Silkey Schultze.

Registration costs $75. Admission is free for BCC students, faculty and staff. To register, visit berkshirecc.edu/summit.

The event is sponsored by BFAIR, a human services agency serving people with disabilities and their families.
